children: By Bharath Rajeswaran

Indian shares rose on Thursday as bargain buying emerged after the recent selloff, with banks and financials leading gains, while a hawkish U.S. Federal Reserve, elevated oil prices, and a crowded IPO market capped the upside.
The Nifty 50
rose 0.26% to 23,279.45, while the BSE Sensex added 0.16% to 74,452.88, as of 10:40 a.m. IST.
Fourteen of the 16 major sectors posted gains. The broader small-cap
and mid-cap
rose 0.7% each.
IT index
fell 0.7%, as higher U.S. interest rates could curb corporate technology spending in the United States, a key market for Indian software exporters.
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points in a unanimous decision overnight, its first increase in more than three years.
Its updated quarterly projections showed 16 of 18 policymakers expected at least one more 25-bp increase by year-end.
Brent crude
eased slightly to about $106 a barrel after reports that Saudi Arabia was offering additional cargoes through Oman, easing immediate supply concerns.
The benchmarks have risen for two sessions after falling more than 1% on Tuesday, extending a near-5% decline over the previous five weeks.
After several sessions of weakness, oversold market conditions have prompted short-covering and selective bargain buying, said Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of HST Wealth.
"The retreat in Brent from recent highs offers limited relief, but the Fed's rate increase and signal of further tightening could sustain volatility and cap any near-term recovery."
Banks
, financials (.NIFPVTBNK) and state-owned lenders
rose 0.1%, 0.3% and 0.4%, respectively.

The Fed's move strengthened expectations of tighter domestic policy, which could support lenders' near-term net interest margins as loan yields generally reprice faster than deposit costs, two traders said.
Among stocks, Turtlemint Fintech
surged 6.4% after Motilal Oswal initiated coverage with a "Buy" rating and forecast 41% upside.
Emami
climbed 5% after Goldman Sachs reiterated its "Buy" call, citing core-business growth and relatively inexpensive valuations.
